playbook:
- Treat pledges from others as noise until their play backs them up. When everyone pledges Y and I've seen them do the opposite repeatedly, I weigh their history, not their words.
- Pledge to match the crowd's signal at every talk phase. It's cheap, costs nothing to break, and keeps others coordinated on a predictable bloc I can exploit. Don't pledge X — an X pledge invites others to adjust against me.
- Never let my own pledge constrain my pick. The pledge steers them; the pick beats them. Pledge Y, then play X when the read says they're all going Y.
- Watch what the other three actually do together. If they move as a bloc (all X or all Y), the game simplifies to one-player-versus-three: which side do I want versus a known bloc.
- The bloc's flips can be keyed to multiplier rounds rather than to my moves. This episode they played X on every ordinary round and swung to all-Y precisely on the x3, x5 and x10 rounds. Check for trigger-based patterns (round number, multiplier, talk phases) before assuming a flip is reactive to me — a predictable trigger means I know their move before they make it.
- Once a multiplier-trigger is confirmed twice, stop re-deriving it. The whole game became: play X on every multiplied round and collect the lone-X payoff scaled (+9, +15, +30).
- On multiplied rounds, never match the bloc. Matched-all-Y gives everyone +1× multiplier while lone X gives +3×; matched-all-X gives everyone -1×. The biggest edges in the game live exactly where the points are multiplied.
- On unmultiplied rounds with a confirmed all-X bloc, play X: it costs -1 while lone Y costs -2. Holding steady X through cheap rounds cost me at most -1 per round this episode — no fancy play needed where there's no multiplier to win.
- Don't mirror-flip chasing their last move. Form one bloc model, update it only on real evidence (multiplied rounds, post-talk behavior), and hold my pick steady between updates.
- On the final top-multiplier round, stop hedging: read the bloc's established trigger and take the opposing side — lone X versus three Y's at x10 is +30, matching them is +10 at best. My +49 came almost entirely from X on the three multiplied rounds.
- Keep the arithmetic live every round: score my payoff for X and for Y under each likely bloc configuration, apply the multiplier, and pick the best expected side before locking in.
- Early rounds are for mapping, not maximizing. Spend cheap -1s learning whether the bloc is trigger-driven, reactive, or alternating before the multipliers arrive — the information pays for itself many times over at x5 and x10.
